easy.def: Wanting to do something very much.
examples: I am eager to see my friends.
The dog is eager for a walk.
We were eager to open our gifts.

more.def: Very excited and interested in doing or having something.
examples: The puppies were eager to go outside and play.
The eager students raised their hands before the question ended.
He was eager to show his parents his report card.
The earthquake made the house shake.
We hid under the desk in the earthquake.
An earthquake can crack a road.

more.def: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement deep inside the Earth.
examples: The earthquake knocked books off the shelves.
The bridge was built to stay standing in an earthquake.
Scientists measure how strong each earthquake is.

easy.def: A sound that comes back to you.
examples: I yelled in the cave and heard an echo.
The big empty room has an echo.
I love to hear my echo in the tunnel.

more.def: A sound you hear again because it bounces off a surface like a wall or cliff.
examples: We shouted across the canyon and listened for the echo.
The echo of footsteps filled the empty hallway.
Bats listen for echoes to find insects.
It takes effort to learn to read.
Thank you for your effort.
Cleaning my room took a lot of effort.

more.def: The energy and hard work you use to do something.
examples: With a lot of effort, they pushed the heavy sled up the hill.
The whole team made an effort to welcome the new player.
It took real effort to carry the canoe to the lake.

easy.def: To make someone feel shy or silly.
examples: It would embarrass me to sing alone.
Please do not embarrass me in front of my friends.
My loud hiccups embarrassed me.

more.def: To make someone feel awkward or ashamed in front of others.
examples: Tripping on stage embarrassed him, but he kept going.
He did not mean to embarrass his sister by telling the story.
Forgetting her lines embarrassed the young actor.

easy.def: Someone who does not like you and wants to hurt you.
examples: The hero beat his enemy.
The cat and the dog are not enemies.
The mouse ran from its enemy.

more.def: A person or group that is against you or wants to harm you.
examples: In the story, the two enemies finally became friends.
Rust is the enemy of old bikes left in the rain.
The two kingdoms had been enemies for a hundred years.

easy.def: What you need to move, play, and grow.
examples: Food gives me energy to run.
The sun gives us energy.
I have no energy today. I need a nap.

more.def: The power that makes things move, work, grow, or give off heat and light.
examples: Solar panels turn energy from the sun into electricity.
The puppy has so much energy that it never sits still.
Wind turbines turn moving air into energy.
I enjoy playing in the snow.
We enjoy the park.
Did you enjoy the movie?

more.def: To get pleasure or happiness from something.
examples: We enjoyed the concert so much that we clapped for five minutes.
My grandfather enjoys working in his garden.
I enjoyed meeting your cousins at the picnic.
An elephant is enormous.
We ate an enormous pizza.
The whale has an enormous tail.
An enormous wave crashed over the rocks.
The library has an enormous collection of books.
An enormous tree had fallen across the road.

easy.def: The land, water, and air around us.
examples: We keep the environment clean.
Trash hurts the environment.
Fish need a clean environment.

more.def: The natural world of land, water, air, plants, and animals around us.
examples: Planting trees is one way to help the environment.
Riding a bike instead of driving is better for the environment.
Oil spills cause great harm to the ocean environment.
The hamster tried to escape from its cage.
The bird escaped out the window.
We escaped from the rain.

more.def: To get free from a place or from danger.
examples: The fish escaped through a hole in the net.
The people escaped the burning building through the back door.
Hot air escapes when you leave the door open.

easy.def: To look at something very closely.
examples: The doctor will examine my ear.
I examine the bug with my eyes.
The vet examines our dog.

more.def: To look at or check something carefully to learn more about it.
examples: We examined the leaf under a magnifying glass.
The detective examined the room for clues.
She examined the coin closely to read its date.
I was exhausted after the long walk.
The exhausted baby fell asleep.
We were exhausted after the swim.

more.def: Extremely tired, with no energy left.
examples: After the race, the exhausted runners lay down on the grass.
The exhausted hikers finally reached their camp.
I was exhausted from staying up too late.

easy.def: A test to find out something.
examples: We did an experiment with ice and salt.
In our experiment, the egg floated.
The experiment made bubbles.

more.def: A careful test done to discover or prove something.
examples: Our science experiment showed that plants grow toward light.
The scientist repeated the experiment to check her results.
As an experiment, we tried baking the bread without sugar.

easy.def: To look around a new place.
examples: Let's explore the garden!
We explore the beach for shells.
The cat explores the new house.

more.def: To travel through or look carefully at a place to learn about it.
examples: The divers explored a cave deep under the sea.
Robots explore the surface of Mars.
On vacation, we explored the old part of the city.

easy.def: No longer living anywhere on Earth.
examples: Dinosaurs are extinct.
Some animals may go extinct.
The extinct bird had a big beak.

more.def: No longer existing; having no living members left.
examples: The dodo bird became extinct hundreds of years ago.
Woolly mammoths have been extinct for thousands of years.
People are working to keep tigers from becoming extinct.
